notes: No genuine Bestsellers-type PLP exists on serenaandlily.com. Checked: (1) the site's full main-nav mega-menu (extracted from the homepage's own Next.js __NEXT_DATA__ at props.pageProps.globalContent.headerV2.slideOutMenu.categoryMenu.menuItems via curl_cffi impersonate=chrome124, HTTP 200) - every top-level menu (New, Furniture, Outdoor, Bedding, Bath, Rugs, Lighting, Wallpaper, Pillows & Throws, Decor, Kids, Art, Clearance, Design) and every submenu item was enumerated; none is named or resembles Bestsellers/Best Sellers/Top Sellers/Popular/Most Popular/Trending/Customer Favorites. A string search of the full homepage __NEXT_DATA__ JSON for 'best-seller','bestseller','top-seller','popular','trending' returned zero matches. (2) The gzipped category sitemap (https://www.serenaandlily.com/sitemap.xml.gz, 500+ URLs) was searched case-insensitively for best-seller|bestseller|top-seller|popular|trending|customer-favorite - zero matches. (3) The site's robots.txt/llm-index.json gave no additional hints; sitemap-0.xml (static pages) has no bestsellers-style page either. (4) Two sitemap-only candidates that superficially resemble 'Customer Favorites' were opened and rejected: /category/most-favorited (CMS-internal name 'Most Favorited') and /category/serena-and-lily-favorites (CMS-internal name 'Welcome Email Favorites 2'). Neither is linked from the current main nav or homepage content (confirmed via full-text search of the homepage JSON - only '/favorites' appears, which is the personal wishlist icon/link, not a merchandising PLP). Sibling sitemap entries in the same naming family (welcome-email-favorites, reels-new-home-favorites, most-favorited, labor-day-favorites, thank-you-favorites, spring-favorites-2024, 2025-fall-design-favorites) are clearly one-off email/social/seasonal marketing-curation snapshots tied to specific campaigns, not an evergreen site-taxonomy Bestsellers concept the nav or category tree recognizes - so these were excluded rather than recorded as ambiguous rows. Access notes: direct category-page fetches via curl_cffi (impersonate=chrome124) return HTTP 200 with full SSR HTML+__NEXT_DATA__ (nav/CMS content only - the product grid itself is fetched client-side post-hydration via a GraphQL call requiring a browser-minted session token, confirmed in the prior Home-Decor pass); headless Playwright is hard-blocked by DataDome (HTTP 403 on every URL tried, including the homepage and every candidate); Claude-in-Chrome was attempted as the tier-3 last resort but the shared browser session repeatedly lost/reassigned its tab group between calls (observed foreign tabs from other concurrent workers), making it unusable this session after one successful page load. None of this affects the Bestsellers conclusion since the absence finding here rests on nav/sitemap taxonomy, not on qty extraction.
